summary: The result group gives a machine-checked example for a question Grünbaum published in Math. Intelligencer (2010). The question is precisely stated and attributed, its source checks out, and it has a clear audience in discrete geometry and tilings (parallelohedra, zonohedra, golden-rhombohedron structures in quasicrystal geometry). The account of prior examples is incomplete in a way that matters. The same four-dimple solid that the submission credits to Inchbald (web, by March 2023) was published as a lattice space-filler by David Hall on Sketchfab in June 2016. So the earliest known example of this family predates the one the submission cites by about seven years. The submission claims no priority, and GET A remains a distinct, newly checked witness.

findings.message: The account names Inchbald's dimpled rhombic triacontahedron (on the web by March 2023) as the earlier k = 10 example of this family. That is not the earliest such source. A Sketchfab model by David Hall, dated 28 June 2016, presents a 'Dimpled Rhombic Triacontahedron': a rhombic triacontahedron with one golden rhombohedron removed at each of four tetrahedrally placed vertices. It is described as chiral, as a 'space filling polyhedron' and as packing 'to form a lattice'. This appears to be the same solid as Inchbald's, the one with 12 rotational symmetries. The public account of prior work should cite Hall (2016) as the earliest known appearance of this family, and the Inchbald dating in 'What is claimed' should be revised to match. Related web constructions should also be checked and disclosed, notably J. Kostick's vZome pages of 2022 showing tetrahedrally and octahedrally dimpled triacontahedra filling space. The k = 10 zone property and Grünbaum's question are not mentioned in these sources. GET A itself was not found in them.

internal_notes.message: Positive: the open-problem quotation, the 'No information is available for any k ≥ 10' sentence, the remark that no other indentations of F or T 'seem to be parallelohedra', the spherical-type convention and the parallelohedron definition all match the submission's quotations. The citation is accurate.

Notability: an explicit, proved example for a published open question (k = 10 was stated to have no information), with a precise statement in Grünbaum's own terms (grunbaum_k10_parallelohedron) and a stronger lattice face-to-face form. Plausibly a serious research note in discrete geometry and tilings, with an identifiable audience: researchers on parallelohedra and zonohedra, the Senechal–Taylor line of work, and crystallography of golden rhombohedra. The calibration theorems are routine and serve only as checks on the definition, which is appropriate. Interest beyond specialists is not shown, so this is not an unusually consequential result. The 2016 and 2023 web appearances of a solid in the same family reduce the novelty of the bare existence claim at k = 10. They do not remove the research interest: none of them links the solid to zones or to Grünbaum's question, gives a proof, or presents GET A.

Hall's tetrahedrally dimpled triacontahedron, if it is a translation parallelohedron as Inchbald and the submitter's computation indicate, is also a counterexample to Grünbaum's remark that no other indentations of T seem to be parallelohedra. Whether this is the 'counterexample to a statement by Grünbaum' in Senechal–Taylor (2023) could not be determined: the abstract says only that their three solids come from skeletons of Fedorov's parallelohedra. The disclosed correspondence says GET A/B are not among them. Not a finding, since the full text is closed access and the submission discloses that it was not read.

The PubMed page did not render for the tool. The search snippet confirms the abstract content as the submission summarises it (three new nonconvex parallelohedra; a counterexample to a statement by Grünbaum). The unread full text and the private correspondence are disclosed precisely, and no priority is claimed from them. Under the policy this is a tooling and evidence limitation, not a finding.

Hall says the DRTs 'can be packed to form a lattice' and that 'fourteen such DRTs will completely enclose one'. That is consistent with a translation lattice tiling, but it is not stated explicitly as translation-only. The submitter's own exact check of Inchbald's solid (same family) supports the tiling.

The Inchbald steelpillow page was not reached at the guessed URL, so the dating via the Internet Archive was not re-verified. The Kabai Wolfram Demonstration '54-Faced Space-Filling Polyhedron' (parts of a rhombic triacontahedron) appeared in search but was not opened. It is likely not rhombic monohedral with 30 faces, so it is a plausible comparison only. No systematic search of other proof libraries (Isabelle AFP, Coq, HOL Light) for formalized parallelohedra was done here either. The submission discloses the same limit.

what_would_reach_higher: Cite D. Hall, 'Dimpled Rhombic Triacontahedron' (Sketchfab, 28 June 2016) as the earliest known web appearance of the four-dimple, tetrahedrally placed space-filling triacontahedron. Revise the Inchbald paragraph and the 'What is claimed' sentence so they no longer imply that Inchbald (by March 2023) is the earliest example.

Check and disclose related web constructions: J. Kostick's vZome sharing pages (2022) on tetrahedrally and octahedrally dimpled triacontahedra filling space, and the Kabai 54-faced space-filler. State for each whether it is rhombic monohedral, of spherical type, and a translation parallelohedron, and whether it gives k = 10.

State explicitly that Hall's and Inchbald's tetrahedrally dimpled triacontahedron also appears to contradict Grünbaum's remark that no other indentations of T 'seem to be parallelohedra'. Say whether this may be the counterexample in Senechal–Taylor (2023), and state the uncertainty, since the full text is unread.

Obtain the full text of Senechal–Taylor (2023) by a free route (author copy, or a request to the authors) and replace the private-correspondence disclosure with a checked description of their three solids and the Grünbaum statement they contradict.

Run and record a brief search of other proof libraries (Isabelle AFP, Coq/Rocq, HOL Light, Mizar) for formalized parallelohedra, zonohedra or belts, so that the prior-formalization statement rests on a search rather than on 'to the submitter's knowledge'.

To widen the notability case: address k ≥ 12 (even partially, e.g. a construction or an obstruction), or give a classification of all k = 10 witnesses within the four-indentation family of the triacontahedron (GET A, GET B, the Hall/Inchbald solid), proved in Lean, including the non-congruence of GET A and GET B, which is currently checked outside Lean.
